models.bounds: Two distinct database/region/queue scopes; one queue creation and one message per scope; at most two receives per message; clock 0..2, delay/visibility 0..1, retention two abstract ticks, two attribute configurations. Cached HTTP queue lookup can interleave with queue deletion. Deleted message/queue row metadata is normalized to zero. Receipt candidates include current, previous, unissued and peer handles; baseline equality admits only the current handle.
models.limits: Atomic transition abstraction after the native parent/expiry/rollback repair. Scopes abstract separately configured database/region/queue targets, not selected IAM principals. Receipt freshness assumes collision-free opaque IDs. No SQL/Go refinement, cryptographic proof, restart/file durability, wall-clock or long-poll liveness, batch/multiple-message atomicity, FIFO/exactly-once/distributed replica behavior, Unicode/size/checksum correctness or full URL validation. Queue name reuse beyond one lifetime is outside the bound; native regression tests separately cover actual storage failures and persistence.

models.bounds: Two trusted queue scopes; three possible pre-existing row IDs plus one additional fresh ID; each row weight1–2 abstract payload units. MaxRows2/MaxBytes3. Initial unique-ID row sets include legacy states with3rows and up to6units, beyond either cap. Initial enumeration uses the exact729 unique-ID assignments, not a powerset filter. No time transition: expiry is a pre-existing Boolean classification.
models.limits: Finite physical-payload budget abstraction, not Go/SQLite refinement, SQL transaction/crash proof, Unicode/UTF8/string-byte counting, JSON attribute serialization, actual64MiB/10000row arithmetic, file size/SQLite overhead, clock/retention, receipt/IAM authorization or random-ID collision resistance. Row weights abstract persisted body+serialized-attribute bytes; all foreign rows, including expired ones, consume budget. Scopes/parent queues are assumed already valid and trusted; SQSLifecycle/native tests separately handle authority, parent lifetime and receipts. Maintenance enabledness assumes these preconditions, not unauthorized access or liveness/fairness. Charged counters describe successful admission accounting, not a claim that an actual storage-error path computed counters. FailedSendPreservesRows still applies to every rejected/storage-error send. Legacy overcap rows are retained: only new accepted sends must fit both caps, own expired cleanup is explicit/scoped and rollback preserves every row on send failure.

models.bounds: 2 browser clients, 3 fresh opaque browser tokens, 1 operator and 1 participant SDK credential; integer clock0..3, browserTTL2,parentTTL1; login only while expiry fits boundedclock
models.limits: One Access authority; opaque disjoint fresh tokens abstract hash storage/randomness. Clock0..3/browserTTL2/participantTTL1 and login cutoff bound exploration, not API limits. No Go/cryptographic/locking/HTTP-Origin/TLS/cookie/UI/accessibility/cross-team refinement or liveness proof. UI and named tests are caller/correspondence seams, not code executed or proven by TLC; actual native/browser assertions independently check them.

models.bounds: Two abstract queue/context labels, epochs0..1 with no wrap, one abstract response/receipt per context+epoch; finite pending/display/custody and captured acceptance history.
models.limits: Finite view acceptance/custody abstraction only, not React/AbortController/DOM/thread execution, token authentication, IAM, native receipt validity/freshness, Go/SQL, cryptography or AWS visual parity. Native requests may finish after cancellation; only current replies enter the view. Accepted history captures its original mounted/context/epoch, so later changes cannot relabel an old acceptance. Unmount epoch advance is redundant with the alive guard and the combined mutant deliberately removes both. Receipt values abstract one response identity per context/epoch; native freshness and release require actual browser/SDK tests. main.jsx source scope is only added SQS keyed-remount/navigation seam, not all other services or authentication.
